newsitem.title: USA: FAA orders flight recorders to collect more data.
newsitem.headline: FAA orders flight recorders to collect more data.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Thursday ordered more information be collected by digital flight data recorders, a move that should aid accident investigations.

The new rule will have its greatest safety impact on aircraft manufactured before 1991 with more than 30 seats. The number of flight parameters recorded will leap to 17 or 18 versus the current 11, FAA said in a statement.
The National Transportation Safety Board had recommended the upgrading of the flight recorders for several years.
NTSB had said the lack of data hampered investigations into two crashes of older Boeing 737 aircraft, the most recent being the crash of USAir Flight 427 near Pittsburgh in 1994.
The FAA ruling will also have a dramatic effect on aircraft manufactured in the future with the number of flight parameters recorded going to 57 and then 88 parameters from the current 29.
For existing planes, retrofits will be made within the next four years during major maintenance checks. Estimated cost for larger aircraft affected by the order is $5,611 each, FAA said.
